title: Somemore Taylor
goal: Use the famous Maclaurin series (centered at $a = 0$) for $e^x$, $\sin x$, $\cos x$, $\frac{1}{1-x}$, and $\ln(1+x)$ as Lego blocks to build new Taylor polynomials without taking endless derivatives.

beforeThis.skill: Instead of differentiating $e^{-x^2}$ six times, just take the known pattern $e^u = 1 + u + \frac{u^2}{2!} + \frac{u^3}{3!} + \cdots$ and plug in $u = -x^2$!

seeIt.title: Taylor series (Ch. 11 of Essence of Calculus)
seeIt.creator: 3Blue1Brown
seeIt.watchFor: Visualizes the standard Maclaurin polynomials for $\cos x$, $\sin x$, and $e^x$.

slowWalkthrough.title: Calculus 2 Lecture 9.9: Approximation of Functions by Taylor Polynomials
slowWalkthrough.creator: Professor Leonard

questions.asking: Add the known Maclaurin series for $\sin x$ (odd powers) and $\cos x$ (even powers) up to the $x^{16}$ term—no differentiating needed!
questions.statement: Give the 16th-order Maclaurin polynomial for $f(x) = \sin x + \cos x$.

questions.asking: Replace $e^x$, $\sin x$, and $\cos x$ with their Maclaurin polynomials up to degree $3$ to find the exact limit as $x \to 0$.
questions.statement: Use Maclaurin polynomials to evaluate $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{e^x - \sin x - \cos x - x^2}{x^3}$.

questions.asking: Write the 5th-degree Maclaurin polynomial for $6\arctan x$ and evaluate it at a known special-angle input to estimate $\pi$.
questions.statement: Use a 5th-order Maclaurin polynomial for $6\arctan x$ to approximate $\pi$.
